name: ActivityNet
description: A large-scale video benchmark for human activity understanding. Provides samples from 203 activity classes with an average of 137 untrimmed videos per class and 1.41 activity instances per video, for a total of 849 video hours. The benchmark covers a wide range of complex human activities that are of interest to people in their daily living and can be used to compare algorithms for three scenarios: untrimmed video classification, trimmed activity classification, and activity detection.
evaluation_method: mAP (mean Average Precision) for detection; accuracy for classification
typical_sota_score: ~90%+ accuracy for trimmed classification; ~60–75 mAP for temporal detection
reputation: Foundational large-scale video understanding benchmark; introduced at CVPR 2015; ActivityNet Challenge has been run annually since 2016; widely used for video classification, temporal localization, and dense video captioning
notes: Introduced at CVPR 2015. 28,108 video clips from 203 activity classes. Annual challenge organized in conjunction with CVPR. Covers both classification and temporal activity detection tasks. Also includes ActivityNet Captions dataset for dense video captioning. Widely used as a foundation benchmark in video understanding research.

institutions: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
